post.description: Always succeeds in shape, even for an address that already exists — confirming that would let anyone enumerate accounts. A verification email follows.
Rate limited per IP **and** per email — an attacker rotating IPs against one account still burns the per-email budget.
Presenting a token that was already rotated revokes the whole family — the standard signal that a refresh token was stolen.
Always 202, whether or not the address exists.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token

get.description: The resolved context: identity, membership, and the permissions held right now. Resolved per request, so a revoked grant disappears immediately.
get.summary: Who am I, and what may I do

post.description: Audited: an insurer is the parent every office inherits its currency, locale and time zone from, so its creation is a platform-level change worth recording.

get.summary: List every KPM on the platform

post.description: The only way an office comes into existence — there is no self-service path (ADR-0005). Seeds the per-office settings every prototype screen hardcodes.

patch.description: Name the person by email or by user id. The account must already exist — this promotes an existing platform user; inviting a new one arrives with invitations in Phase 3. Audited with both the outgoing and incoming user.
patch.summary: Assign or transfer the KPM Owner

patch.description: A suspended office refuses its members with TENANT_SUSPENDED, distinct from a permission failure so the UI can explain it.
patch.summary: Suspend, reactivate or archive a KPM

get.description: Defaults to the caller's own tenant. A Super Admin has no tenant, so their default is the platform-level log — provisioning, company creation, impersonation — and `kpmId` narrows it to one office. Anyone else is pinned to their own office whatever they pass.

parameters.name: kpmId
parameters.description: Super Admin only: narrow the log to one office. Omitted reads the platform-level log. Ignored for anyone else, who always reads their own office.

post.description: Time-boxed to an hour, reason required, and every action it produces records both the real Super Admin and the person acted as. Refused for another Super Admin — that would erase the attribution the feature depends on.

get.description: Each row carries whether you may change that person's role. The rule is a server rule, and sending the answer stops the screen keeping a second copy of it that can drift out of step.
get.summary: The people who report to you

patch.description: Agent ⇄ AAB is the direct leader's call. Anything involving AB is the Owner's or an Admin's. Nobody moves: a role change is a statement about a person, not a reorganisation. Demoting somebody who still leads people is refused with the count, so the caller knows what has to happen first.

get.description: Read from the append-only membership history, which is the only place the before-and-after of a role survives.

delete.description: Requires the literal word REMOVE in the body — the screen's gate is a convenience, this is the control. Nothing is deleted: the row, the agent code and every history event stay with the office. If they still have reports, the body must say where those reports go; there is no default, because a default here silently reorganises somebody else's unit.

get.description: Someone outside your scope reads as 404 — a 403 would confirm they exist.

A flat node list plus the ids of its roots. Narrowed exactly as the roster is: a tenant admin sees the office, everybody else sees themselves and their downline. The answer is a **forest** — a root is any visible node whose leader is not also visible, which is the office root plus anybody orphaned by a removal or not yet tagged. Your own leader comes back separately and is not a node, so it cannot be given a layer. Refuses rather than truncates above the cap: a page of a tree is not a tree.
Readable by the Owner and by Admins — knowing who else administers the office is not a power, and hiding it would make the nav lie. Each row says whether the reader may revoke it.

post.description: Owner only. An Admin attempting it is refused with PERM_OWNER_ONLY rather than a flat PERM_DENIED — they are told the Owner reserved it. Admin rights are orthogonal to hierarchy role: an AB with a unit of forty can hold them.

delete.description: Owner only. The Owner’s own access comes from being the Owner, not from a grant, and cannot be revoked — transferring the office is the operation for that.

get.description: Tags this office defines for its own organising — a mentoring circle, a task force. Never hierarchy and never access: nothing in scope resolution reads them.

put.summary: Rename a group, or hand it to a different owner

delete.description: Archived, never deleted, and the tags on the people who were in it stay. The prototype splices the row and strips everybody’s tags in the same breath, so the record that a cohort existed is gone.

get.summary: What this person is tagged with

put.description: Core Leader gates Strategic Leader Forum co-editing (Phase 14) and nothing else — no hierarchy, no data scope. A group is the same: a label, not a rule.
put.summary: Set this person’s groups and Core Leader flag

get.description: Cursor-paginated by agent code. Filter by role and status, or search by name, email or agent code. Removed members are excluded unless asked for.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name, email or agent code. Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Omitted excludes removed members — the roster asks who is here now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page — an agent code.

get.description: One level down. The whole downline is the tree endpoint, not this one.
Office, leader and any outstanding request. Answers for somebody in no office too — that is a valid state, not an error.

The only cross-tenant read a non-Super-Admin has, and the reason it exists is that otherwise nobody could join. Projection-limited to code, branch name, company and city: no member counts, no production, no owner name.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Office code or branch name. Case-insensitive substring.

post.description: Creates a pending membership with no leader — inside the office, in the untagged pool, with no unit-scoped grants at all. A leader still has to take you on.

get.description: Everyone in your office holding AB or AAB. By role rather than by the graph: this asks who may take you on, and a new AAB has to be askable to ever get a first report.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name only, as the prototype searches it.

post.description: Notifies them; they decide. Asking somebody else replaces the outstanding ask rather than adding a second — two open rows would let two approvers both say yes.
post.summary: Ask a leader to take you

get.description: Revoked and spent ones stay in the list, so you can see what has been out there rather than only what still works.

post.description: Returns the code and the link; a QR is that link rendered. Anyone who redeems it joins your office tagged to you, with no approval — which is why it can carry a use limit and an expiry, and can be revoked.

delete.description: Kills the code, the link and the QR at once — they are one artefact.

get.description: Whose unit and which office, so somebody can see what they are accepting before they accept it. Unknown, revoked and expired all answer alike.
Includes anything routed to you by somebody above — an AB may send an agent into one of their AABs' units, and that AAB is then the one who decides.
Your own direct AABs, and only those. Empty for an AAB — their reports are agents, so there is no sub-unit below them.
get.summary: Units you may send somebody into

post.description: Returns the inbox as it now stands. Deciding one that was already decided is a 409 naming which way it went — two leaders can have this open at once.
They stay registered to the office and may ask somebody else. Declining is not removal, and the reason is sent to them.

get.description: Office-wide, because somebody untagged belongs to nobody yet and so cannot be found by looking down anybody's tree.
get.summary: People in this office with no leader

post.description: No approval from them — the office already admitted them, and being placed under a leader is not a change they have standing to refuse. Somebody who already reports to another leader is refused: moving them is a different operation.
post.summary: Add an untagged person to your unit

post.description: Registers you and tags you to the issuer in one step, with no approval — that is the whole difference from asking a leader. No join request is created: one would sit in their inbox asking them to approve something that already happened.

info.title: AgencyBoost API
info.description: Multi-tenant SaaS for insurance agency offices (KPM)

refreshToken.description: Only for non-browser clients. A browser sends the httpOnly cookie set at login and should omit this entirely.

token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Expires in 15 minutes.

pronoun.description: Yours to set. It appears in the coaching commitment sentence your leader reads.

code.description: Unique within the company. Prefixes agent codes.

timezone.description: Canonical for every day boundary in this office. Inherited from the company if omitted.

email.description: The account to make Owner. It must already exist — create one at /register or with POST /auth/register. Email is what a Super Admin normally knows.

userId.description: Alternative to email, for when you already have the id.

reason.description: Recorded in the audit log. Required.

reason.example: Ready to bring on their own agents
reason.description: Kept in the role change log, which is the only place this can be read back.

action.description: Where the reports of the person being removed go. There is no default: leaving it to the server would be a silent reorganisation of somebody else’s unit.

toMembershipId.description: Required when action is `reassign`. The membership their reports move to.

confirmation.description: The literal word REMOVE, trimmed and case-insensitive. Checked here as well as in the screen — a confirmation only the screen enforces is not a confirmation.

reason.description: Kept on the removal history event, and sent to them.

subtree.description: Required when they still have direct reports; refused otherwise.

ownerMembershipId.description: The membership that owns it. Never a name — the prototype stores `ownerName`, which breaks the moment anybody is renamed or two people share one.

groupIds.description: Every live group this person should be in. Absent ids are removed; tags on retired groups are kept, because they are the record that a cohort existed.

isCoreLeader.description: Gates Strategic Leader Forum co-editing (Phase 14) and nothing else. It grants no hierarchy and no data scope.

label.description: A note for you. Never shown to whoever redeems it.

maxUses.description: How many people may use it. Omitted means no ceiling.

expiresInDays.description: Days until it stops working. Omitted means it runs until revoked.

routeToMembershipId.description: One of your own AABs, from GET /join/requests/routing. Omitted adds them to your own unit. Ignored for an AB or AAB requester — a leader is not placed in a unit, they are tagged to you directly.

reason.example: Not in my patch — try Sari
reason.description: Sent to them. The prototype captures none, which leaves a decline unexplainable.

code.description: From a link, a QR, or read aloud.
